Resolves #21660

One held ARC-17 card compares two real telescope slots. North yields 600 simulated samples while its detector readout pushes the neighbouring mosaic back eight minutes. South collects 240 samples without moving that programme. Holding a late slot explains the missed ingress. The visitor can inspect the resulting Gantt, book an option, and run the simulated observation.

Evidence: L3 on the real Board, Scheduler and Gantt in headless Chrome. L3 required for held geometry, admission, withdrawal and visible geometry after release.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Receipt |
| --- | --- |
| F1 · compare before release | One native pointer crosses North → South → late. The slot outline, physical drag tooltip, linked Gantt geometry and fixed-window signal update while the committed observing plan retains its records and revision. |
| F2 · commit, cancel and stale state | The accepted release publishes one revision. Escape, a denied slot and withdrawing clearance while still held leave bookings intact. Native keyboard controls compare before committing. |
| F3 · simulated acquisition | The film distinguishes the predicted flux from individually sampled values. An explicit run replays the four-minute acquisition, including the two-minute occultation; reduced motion shows the complete sample set. |
| B1 · visible planning surfaces | The opening places the native request board beside the resource schedule and the light curve beside the native dependency chart. The fixed UTC event band appears on both timelines. |
| B2 · rescheduling | A booked exposure can move through the native Scheduler writer. Its crew card and timing readout follow. |
| B3 · native Gantt cascade | Moving Guide lock moves the exposure and readout. On North the mosaic and its processing successor also move, and missing ingress disables observation. |
| B4 · crew clearance | The native Board can withdraw or reinstate ARC-17 clearance. A direct status change cannot create a telescope reservation. |
| B5 · find and replay | Reset returns the night to its original state. The record is in Scheduler, Gantt and Task Board and has explicit source, development, ESM and production entries. |

## Deltas from ticket

The bounded five-task forecast uses distinct task and dependency stores with the same native Gantt writer. A thin tick marks each affected task’s committed start. The reusable engine-level cascade projection remains under discussion in #21664. The two telescopes, frame rates and astronomical event are simulated. The masthead uses an original generated image.

## Test Evidence

- `MeridianPointer.spec.mjs` exercises one uninterrupted card drag across actual row/time targets, checks a Gantt bar's painted position, and reads the separate committed plan through the Neural Link.
- `MeridianSequence.spec.mjs` compares forecast/commit pixels for two linked tasks, drives the native Gantt prerequisite by keyboard, checks the phone flow and asserts the top-row alignment.
- All four example builds cold-booted. Each catalog link and its staged 1280×720 cover decoded in Chrome. The companion Pages PR supplies the actual gallery JPEGs. [Cover PR](https://github.com/neomjs/pages/pull/149)

## Cold look

Two independent readers saw the unlabelled full Scheduler page in opposite orders. The reader who saw the change first scored it 8/10 versus 7/10 for the base. The reader who saw the base first gave it 8/10 and the change 9/10. Both kept Studio Bookings as the natural first example and understood the observatory as an additional choice. One needed the card caption to connect the observatory thumbnail to scheduling.

Frame critique: a compact crop cannot show three usable planning widgets. The gallery keeps the observatory and its request card identifiable; the caption names the telescope booking. The full desk shows the actual drag. The source and destination panels share both edges on desktop. On phones they stack at independent heights.

- **Challenge**: Three non-blocking observations from tracing `Viewport.mjs`, `Viewport.css`, and the E2E specs:
  1. **`notice(text)` (`Viewport.mjs:1250`) mutates only `verdictTitle.text`:** During live slot preview (`previewRequest` → `present`), refused slots apply `.meridian-refused` (`--mer-error`) and update `verdictDetail`. However, when a post-booking refusal calls `notice(...)` directly (e.g. dragging `Flux standard` at `ObservationScheduler.mjs:330` or attempting an overlapping `North mosaic` move at `Viewport.mjs:1262` while `ARC-17` is booked), `.meridian-verdict` keeps `.meridian-ok` (mint green border/title) and the previous booking's `verdictDetail` text beside the refusal headline. Resetting `verdict`'s state class to `meridian-refused` (or `meridian-neutral`) and clearing/preserving explicit detail in `notice()` would avoid green-styled refusal text.
  2. **Sequential reactive store writes in `showSequence` (`Viewport.mjs:1046-1048`):** `chart.baseline = ...; chart.store = pair.tasks; chart.dependencyStore = pair.links;` assigns `store` and `dependencyStore` sequentially on the live `Sequence` (`Neo.gantt.Container`) instance before `createViewData(false, true)`.
